ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a large rectangle containing six congruent circles arranged in 3 columns and 2 rows. The circles are tangent to neighboring circles and to the sides of the large rectangle. A smaller rectangle is drawn inside, and its four vertices are located at the centers of the four corner circles. Reasoning: Let the common radius of each circle be r. Since the six circles form a 3-by-2 grid, the large rectangle has width 3 diameters = 6r and height 2 diameters = 4r. The small rectangle spans horizontally from the center of the left corner circle to the center of the right corner circle, which is 2 diameters = 4r. Vertically, it spans from the center of a top corner circle to the center of the corresponding bottom corner circle, which is 1 diameter = 2r. Therefore the small rectangle perimeter is 2(4r + 2r) = 12r. Given 12r = 60, we get r = 5 cm. Thus the large rectangle perimeter is 2(6r + 4r) = 20r = 100 cm.

method.method_draft: Let the common circle radius be r. From the image, the six circles form a 3-by-2 grid inside the large rectangle, tangent to each other and to the outer rectangle. The small rectangle has its four vertices at the centers of the four corner circles. Therefore its width is the distance from the left-column center to the right-column center, equal to 2 diameters = 4r, and its height is the distance from the top-row center to the bottom-row center, equal to 1 diameter = 2r. So its perimeter is 2(4r + 2r) = 12r = 60, giving r = 5. The large rectangle has width 3 diameters = 6r and height 2 diameters = 4r, so its perimeter is 2(6r + 4r) = 20r = 100 cm.
